verdict.rationale: Stripe documents multiple concrete consent mechanisms gating agent spend: Shared Payment Tokens carry scoped usage limits (currency, max amount, expiry) and can be revoked before use; Link CLI requires 'Customers approve each request on the Link website or in the mobile app' before returning a one-time-use credential; and the Stripe MCP server requires human confirmation with an approval token/24-hour expiry before write actions like refunds or outbound payments. These are first-party documented, specific mechanisms rather than vague claims. However, community discussion notes that the machine-payments/MPP rail 'handles how agents pay, but not did anyone authorize this' — meaning per-purchase human consent is not universal across all agentic payment paths, and several of the consent-bearing features (ACS, OCA) are gated as private preview or US/Canada/EU-only. Missing for 10: independent hands-on verification that approval flows work as documented in production, and closing the gap where machine-payments (MPP/x402) lacks a built-in human-authorization step.
